newsitem.title: USA: Great Western stockholders allowed to vote. [CORRECTED 23:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Great Western stockholders allowed to vote. [CORRECTED 23:20 GMT]

text.p: A Delaware judge ruled Tuesday that Great Western Financial Corp shareholders can vote on a proposed stock swap merger with Washington Mutual Inc at the company's June 13 special meeting. (Corrects to show meeting was special, not annual meeting.)
The 41 page ruling by Chancellor Jack Jacobs denied a motion by H.F. Ahmanson & Co that the merger vote be delayed for at least six weeks.
Ahmanson, which has made a competing offer for Great Western, hopes to seat its slate of three directors at the June 13 meeting.
It sought to delay the Great Western meeting to give the new board members enough time to influence the remaining board members to support the Ahmanson offer.
The board has already approved Washington Mutual's offer of 0.9 shares for each Great Western share and voted down Ahmanson's offer of 1.2 shares for each Great Western share.
Both proposals are valued at about $7 billion.

In its request for an injunction against the June 13 merger vote, Ahmanson had argued that "an earlier vote approving the merger (in which Great Western would not survive) would render any election of directors superfluous."

But in his decision, Jacobs said "the result of an injunction would be the delay the ability of Washington Mutual, Great Western and their shareholders to begin realizing the economic benefits expected to result from the merger.

"Delaying the merger would also significantly increase the risk that the value of Great Western would diminish, through losses of customers and key employees as a result of continued uncertainty surrounding the outcome of the bidding contest for control," he continued.

Jacobs also disagreed with Ahmanson's claim that not delaying the merger vote for at least six weeks after the annual meeting would deprive Great Western shareholders of their right to vote for Ahmanson's director nominees.

"If Great Western's shareholders wish to elect Ahmanson's nominees to the board, they need only vote down the Washington Mutual merger proposal at the merger meeting and then vote for the Ahmanson's nominees at the rescheduled annual meeting," he explained. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
